discovery: Cavity optomechanics: quantum control of macroscopic mechanical motion with light, including ground-state cooling

nominees.name: Markus Aspelmeyer
nominees.affiliation: University of Vienna and IQOQI Vienna, Austria

nominees.name: Tobias J. Kippenberg
nominees.affiliation: École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL), Switzerland

motivation: Aspelmeyer, Kippenberg and Painter turned radiation pressure, once only a noise source in precision interferometry, into a tool for quantum control of mechanical objects. Kippenberg demonstrated and explained dynamical backaction and resolved-sideband cooling in optical microresonators. Aspelmeyer pioneered radiation-pressure cooling of micromirrors, strong optomechanical coupling and quantum control of levitated nanoparticles. Painter's optomechanical crystals achieved laser cooling of a mechanical mode to its quantum ground state and showed motional quantum sideband asymmetry. Together they founded a field in which macroscopic mechanical oscillators show quantum behaviour. This includes ponderomotive squeezing, measurement-based feedback, entanglement between light and motion, and quantum-limited force sensing. These methods now underpin quantum-noise reduction in gravitational-wave detectors and transducers for quantum networks. They also open experimental tests of quantum mechanics and gravity at ever larger mass scales.
